clue.text: Difficult time after baby's head is delivered

indicators.note: the head of a word is its front, so only its opening letter is kept

blocks.note: the first letter of baby
a rough time is a difficult one
T is the standard abbreviation for time

explanation.surface: A tough spell for a mother as her baby's head emerges during childbirth.
explanation.walkthrough: 'After' places the difficult time behind the baby's first letter: B, then ROUGH T, giving BROUGHT.
explanation.definitionFit: Something brought has been carried and handed over, which is what a parcel being delivered means.

clue.text: Soldier's prompt resistance brings someone to get us out of trouble

definitions.text: someone to get us out of trouble

blocks.note: RE, the Royal Engineers, are soldiers; the apostrophe-s adds S
a cue prompts an actor
R is the symbol for electrical resistance

explanation.surface: A soldier's quick resistance saves the day by bringing help to people in a tight spot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Prompt' reads as an adjective meaning quick, but it is the noun: a cue.
explanation.definitionFit: A rescuer is a person who saves others from danger or difficulty, exactly the helper described.

clue.text: Employers backing unions' resurgence to some extent

indicators.note: only part of the words is used, so the letters sit inside the run of the clue
going backwards means the concealed letters are read from right to left

blocks.note: the last letter of unions and the first four of resurgence

explanation.surface: Bosses resist the revival of trade unions, at least partly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Employers' looks like bosses, but here it simply means people who employ, or use, something.
explanation.definitionFit: To employ something is to use it, so those who employ a tool or service are its users.

clue.text: Usual practice to have volunteers set up living area

indicators.note: in a down clue, set up means lifted upwards, so the letters read from bottom to top

blocks.note: a habit is something you usually do
TA is the Territorial Army, Britain's volunteer reserve force

explanation.surface: It is normal for volunteers to put up a living space for others.
explanation.definitionFit: A habitat is the natural home or environment where an animal or plant lives.

clue.text: Leaves fellow changing oil to get on

indicators.note: changing the order of letters rearranges them into a new form

blocks.note: F is the abbreviation for fellow
taken as written, then rearranged
to get on is to grow old, to age

explanation.surface: A man walks out after changing the oil, so he can move on.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Leaves' reads as a verb about a fellow departing; it is the noun, the leaves of plants.
explanation.definitionFit: Foliage is the collective word for the leaves of a plant or tree.

clue.text: Goes round renovated bistro

indicators.note: something renovated is done up and rebuilt, so the letters are reassembled

blocks.note: taken as written, then rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone makes the rounds of a newly refurbished little restaurant.
explanation.definitionFit: A planet orbits when it travels in a circular path around a star, circling it repeatedly.

clue.text: Step in when Bury against Everton ends ultimately in violence

indicators.note: the ends of a word are its two outside letters, so only those are taken
ultimately means finally, so only the closing letter of the next word counts

blocks.note: to inter is to bury
V, for versus, means against
the first and last letters of Everton
the final letter of violence

explanation.surface: Someone must step in when a Bury versus Everton football match turns violent.
explanation.walkthrough: Bury and Everton look like football clubs (Bury is a Lancashire town team, Everton a Liverpool one), but Bury is the verb.
explanation.definitionFit: To intervene is to come between parties or get involved to change a situation.

clue.text: Good books contain everything top-class and noble

indicators.note: to contain is to hold inside, so the next words sit within the outer letters

blocks.note: G is the abbreviation for good
all means everything
A is the top grade, as in A1
NT, the New Testament, is a set of books of the Bible

explanation.surface: Fine books hold all that is first-rate and lofty.
explanation.definitionFit: A gallant person is brave and honourable, chivalrous in the way nobility is meant to be.

clue.text: Sort of quite like morning by river, still and noiseless

indicators.note: a sort of something is a variant version, so the letters are rearranged

blocks.note: taken as written, then rearranged
as means like, in comparisons
AM is the abbreviation for morning
the Ouse is a river in England, a crossword favourite

explanation.surface: A calm, silent morning beside a river feels rather peaceful.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom describes someone making no sound at all, as hushed and motionless as a small rodent hiding.

clue.text: Man is one of those I'll report

indicators.note: a report is something spoken and heard, so the word is judged by its sound

blocks.note: the contraction of I will sounds like the island word

explanation.surface: A man declares what he will report.
explanation.walkthrough: Man is the Isle of Man, in the Irish Sea, not a person.
explanation.definitionFit: The Isle of Man is an island, and isle is a poetic or formal word for an island.

clue.text: Tory's contribution to party flyer

blocks.note: blue is the Conservative Party colour, so a Tory is a blue
guests often bring a bottle of wine to a party

explanation.surface: A Conservative politician offers a donation, advertised on a party leaflet.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Party' and 'flyer' suggest political campaigning; the party is a social one and the flyer is an insect.
explanation.definitionFit: A bluebottle is a large buzzing blowfly, and anything that flies can be called a flyer.

clue.text: Evening with film stars ahead

indicators.note: ahead says which piece goes in front when the parts are joined

blocks.note: suns are stars
E.T. is Spielberg's 1982 film

explanation.surface: A night out at the cinema with the celebrities taking the lead.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Film stars' looks like one phrase about actors; split it into film and stars.
explanation.definitionFit: Sunset is the time the sun goes down, marking the start of the evening, so one can stand for the other.

clue.text: Old seabird's regularly able to get outside

indicators.note: regularly means at even intervals, so every other letter is kept

blocks.note: ex means former, old
a tern is a seabird
the first and third letters of able

explanation.surface: An aged seabird can manage to get out of doors.
explanation.definitionFit: External describes what is on the exterior, lying beyond or on the surface of something.

clue.text: Camera set to show off some delights of Cornwall

indicators.note: to show off is to make a display, so the letters are put on display in a new order

blocks.note: taken as written, then rearranged

explanation.surface: A tourist sets up a camera to photograph Cornish treats.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Set' looks like the indicator, but it belongs in the letters; 'show off' does the rearranging.
explanation.definitionFit: Cream teas, scones with clotted cream and jam served with tea, are a famous speciality of Cornwall and Devon in south-west England.

clue.text: May watch a special game at other team's ground

indicators.note: a special version is one made differently, so the letters are reformed

blocks.note: taken as written, then rearranged

explanation.surface: A fan may watch a big game played on the opponents' turf.
explanation.definitionFit: A team plays an away fixture when it travels to the opponents' home stadium rather than its own.

clue.text: Some of meze's typically full of beans

indicators.note: only part of the following words is used, so the letters lie within them

blocks.note: the last three letters of meze's and the first two of typically

explanation.surface: Mezze dishes are usually packed with beans.
explanation.walkthrough: Meze is a spread of small Mediterranean dishes, so beans sound like a literal ingredient.
explanation.definitionFit: Full of beans is an idiom for lively and energetic, which is what zesty means.

clue.text: Holiday snap

blocks.note: first meaning: a short vacation
second meaning: to crack or fracture

explanation.walkthrough: 'Holiday snap' reads as a photo from a trip; the two words are separate meanings.
explanation.definitionFit: A short getaway is a city break or weekend break, and to snap a stick is to fracture it in two.

clue.text: Lease covers to become sick, retired and dependent

indicators.note: retired means gone back, so the word is read in the backward direction
to cover is to wrap around, so one word encloses the other

blocks.note: to lease something is to rent it
to ail is to fall ill

explanation.surface: An insurance lease covers someone who has fallen ill, stopped work and relies on others.
explanation.walkthrough: Retired, sick and dependent all sound like a pensioner; retired is the reversal signal.
explanation.definitionFit: To be reliant on something is to need it and rely upon it for support.

clue.text: Challenged wicked superhero

blocks.note: to dare someone is to challenge them
evil means wicked

explanation.surface: A villain takes on a costumed crime-fighter.
explanation.definitionFit: Daredevil is the blind Marvel comics hero Matt Murdock, so he is an example of the category.

clue.text: Liked to see Joey jumping around in goal

indicators.note: jumping around suggests bouncing about, so the letters are scrambled
in places the jumbled letters inside the word that follows

blocks.note: taken as written, then rearranged
an end is a goal or aim

explanation.surface: A fan loved watching Joey leap about in the goalmouth.
explanation.walkthrough: A joey is also a baby kangaroo, which makes the jumping apt.
explanation.definitionFit: To have enjoyed something is to have taken pleasure in it, as you do with things you like.

clue.text: Dream home in picture

indicators.note: in tells us one word is placed inside the other

blocks.note: an image is a picture
at home means in

explanation.surface: A dream house shown in a photograph.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dream home' looks like a single phrase; Dream is a verb and home goes inside picture.
explanation.definitionFit: To imagine something is to form a picture of it in the mind, as one does when daydreaming.

clue.text: Money received once I'm working

indicators.note: working suggests being worked on, so the letters are reshaped

blocks.note: taken as written, then rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone looks forward to getting paid once they have a job.
explanation.definitionFit: Income is the earnings or payments a person gets from employment or investments.

clue.text: Dance with the French chaps in fine company

indicators.note: in places the preceding words inside the outer pair of letters

blocks.note: F is the abbreviation for fine, on pencils
la is French for the, feminine
chaps are men
Co is the abbreviation for company

explanation.surface: A Frenchwoman dances with some men in good company.
explanation.definitionFit: Flamenco is the passionate Spanish dance from Andalusia with stamping feet and guitar.

clue.text: Spotted cat in car

blocks.note: first meaning: the big cat of Central and South America
second meaning: the British luxury car make

explanation.surface: A cat is noticed sitting inside a vehicle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Spotted' reads as seen; it describes the cat's markings.
explanation.definitionFit: The jaguar is a large spotted wild feline, and Jaguar is also a British make of luxury motor vehicle.

clue.text: Stares open-mouthed at girl taking on monkeys

indicators.note: taking on means adding something more, so the next part is attached behind

blocks.note: G is an abbreviation for girl
apes and monkeys are loosely interchangeable in crosswords

explanation.surface: Onlookers gawp at a girl who is fighting a group of monkeys.
explanation.definitionFit: To gape is to gaze in wonder with the jaw dropped, which is the open-mouthed staring described.

clue.text: In St Lucia you are travelling with care

indicators.note: travelling means moving about, so the letters change places

blocks.note: taken as written, then rearranged

explanation.surface: Advice to a tourist to go carefully when touring the Caribbean island.
explanation.definitionFit: Doing something cautiously means acting carefully to avoid danger or mistakes.

clue.text: Quietly set up goody-goody

blocks.note: p is piano, the musical direction for quietly
to rig is to set up equipment

explanation.surface: A smug self-righteous person is discreetly framed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Set up' is not a reversal here; it means rig, as in setting up a stage.
explanation.definitionFit: A prig is a self-righteous person who behaves as if morally superior to others.

clue.text: The heartless rich I suspect to be more irritating

indicators.note: without its heart, a word loses its central letter and only the outside stays
something suspect is dodgy and not straight, so the letters are rearranged

blocks.note: the outer letters of the
taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone suspects that callous wealthy people are rather annoying.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Suspect' reads as a verb with I as its subject; I is fodder and suspect the signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Itchier means causing a stronger urge to scratch, so more irritating to the skin.

clue.text: Poem about unknown ship on year-long journey

indicators.note: about means around, so the word wraps the next pieces

blocks.note: an ode is a lyric poem
y is an algebraic unknown
SS is steamship
Y is the abbreviation for year

explanation.surface: An epic poem describing a mysterious ship's twelve-month voyage.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Year-long' looks like one word, but year gives a letter and long belongs to the definition. Homer's poem is itself apt.
explanation.definitionFit: An odyssey is any long wandering adventure, named after the ten-year voyage of Odysseus in Homer's epic.
